metrics.label: Population
metrics.description: Resident population.
metrics.method: WorldPop 2020 pixels summed per hex, rescaled so every district (LKA) / county (USA) matches the official 2023 estimate.

metrics.label: Area inside boundary (incl. inland water)
metrics.description: Area inside the national boundary, including lakes, reservoirs and lagoons (sea excluded); the 'land' of land tiles and of population density.
metrics.method: Sum of the areas of WorldPop raster pixels (LKA ~100 m, USA ~1 km) whose centres fall inside the admin boundaries, plus populated pixels that straddle the boundary. Inland water is NOT removed, so the totals exceed official land areas (Sri Lanka 66,074 km2 vs 65,610 km2 total area incl. inland water, World Bank AG.SRF.TOTL.K2; USA 9.30 M km2 vs Census land area ~9.15 M km2).

metrics.label: UNESCO World Heritage Sites
metrics.description: UNESCO World Heritage Sites (cultural, natural and mixed) located in the country.
metrics.method: Wikidata items with P1435 = Q9259 (non-deprecated, no end date) and P17 = country, grouped by the numeric part of the World Heritage Site id (P757; '72bis'/'72ter' -> 72); component items without an id are merged into a site within 3 km. The representative item is the member with the most Wikipedia sitelinks that has a coordinate inside the country grid (coordinates are tried in turn: grid cell, snap within 6 H3 rings, else nearest land hex within 250 km). For natural and mixed sites the coordinate is checked against the site's WDPA 'World Heritage Site (natural or mixed)' polygon (matched by name): a coordinate outside the country (the Yukon point of Kluane / Wrangell-St. Elias, the open-ocean point of Papahanaumokuakea) or more than 2 km outside the polygon (Sinharaja, whose Wikidata point is ~20 km SW of the reserve) is replaced by a representative point of polygon ∩ country (original kept in orig_lat/orig_lon). Sites whose coordinates are all outside the 50 states + DC (US territories, Mexico-only El Camino Real de Tierra Adentro, foreign components of transnational sites) are dropped. kind from the selection criteria (P2614): (i)-(vi) cultural, (vii)-(x) natural, both mixed. inscribed = earliest P580 start time of the designation (year of the original inscription). whs_ref keeps the raw P757 ids; a 'bis'/'ter' suffix (extended_or_modified) marks a later extension or boundary change, so the national component of a transnational site can be younger than `inscribed` (e.g. Moravian Church Settlements, 1468bis).

metrics.label: National park visitors
metrics.description: Annual visitors to national parks (USA: recreation visits; Sri Lanka: ticketed local + foreign visitors).
metrics.method: USA: NPS IRMA Stats Annual Park Ranking Report, calendar year 2025, Recreation Visits, Park Type = National Park (64 units); National Park of American Samoa and Virgin Islands NP (territories) are dropped, leaving 62 parks in the 50 states. Coordinates and area (P2046) from the Wikidata item of each park (instance of Q34918903, matched on normalised names: 'NP' -> National Park, 'NP & PRES' -> National Park and Preserve). US park coordinates more than 5 km outside the park's WDPA polygon (designation 'National Park', exact name match) are moved to a point inside it (Channel Islands: the Wikidata point is in the sea between the islands); original kept in orig_lat/orig_lon. Definitions differ: NPS counts recreation visits (person-entries, estimated from traffic counts for most parks); DWC counts tickets sold.

metrics.label: Museums
metrics.description: Museums with coordinates documented in Wikidata (count of points).
metrics.method: Wikidata items instance of museum (Q33506) or any subclass (art, history, science, house museums...), country P17 = Sri Lanka / United States, with coordinates; items with a dissolution (P576) or closure (P3999) date are dropped, one row per item (first coordinate). Items whose only museum-subclass types are visitor / nature / interpretation centres, heritage railways, film archives, cinematheques or virtual museums are dropped, as are points that do not snap to the country grid (US territories). Duplicate items for one institution are merged (same normalised name within 2 km, or the same coordinate with one name containing the other, e.g. a museum and its 'Main Building' item), keeping the item with most sitelinks. kind = the shortest English label among the item's museum-subclass P31 types other than plain 'museum' (else 'museum'). Coverage reflects Wikidata completeness, not an official museum census (the US IMLS universe lists far more institutions).

metrics.label: Protected area
metrics.description: Share of the hex area covered by designated protected areas (any IUCN category).
metrics.method: Union of WDPCA polygons with status Designated / Inscribed / Established, excluding UNESCO-MAB Biosphere Reserves (Protected Planet convention) and Proposed sites; all IUCN categories incl. 'Not Reported'. Coverage = share of the hex's H3 child-cell centres (res+3 = 343 points per hex for Sri Lanka, res+2 = 49 for the USA) that fall inside any polygon (shapely STRtree). Computed for every grid hex (land and coastal water, 0 where none); marine protected areas count in water hexes. Sri Lanka's polygons are full resolution; US polygons were generalised server-side (maxAllowableOffset 0.005 deg ~ 500 m). WDPA point-only records (no boundary) are not counted.

metrics.label: Strictly protected area (IUCN Ia-IV)
metrics.description: Share of the hex area covered by protected areas in IUCN categories Ia, Ib, II, III or IV.
metrics.method: As protected_pct, restricted to polygons whose iucn_cat is Ia, Ib, II, III or IV (strict reserves, wilderness, national parks, natural monuments, habitat/species management areas). Categories are as reported to WDPA: Sri Lanka reports most Forest Department Reserved Forests as Ib, so its strict share is close to its total share; most US conservation easements and state lands are V or 'Not Assigned'.

metrics.label: Protected area
metrics.description: Area of the hex (land or sea) inside designated protected areas.
metrics.method: protected_pct / 100 x H3 cell area. Overlapping designations are counted once.

metrics.label: GDP (Gold)
metrics.description: Gross domestic product at current prices, US dollars.
metrics.method: USA: BEA CAGDP2, year 2024, current dollars (thousands x 1,000). Lines: total = 1; agriculture = 3 (NAICS 11); industry = 6 + 10 + 11 + 13 + 25 (mining, utilities, construction, durable + nondurable manufacturing); services = total - agriculture - industry (includes government, line 83); manufacturing = 13 + 25 (= line 12); finance = 51 + 56 + 60 (finance & insurance; real estate & rental/leasing; professional, scientific & technical services). Suppressed '(D)' county cells (18,737 in 2024; BEA suppresses complementary cells, so no identity has a single unknown) are estimated for the 20 leaf industries that partition line 2 (private industries) by multi-margin iterative proportional fitting within each state, seeded with ACS 2024 5-year C24030 employment of the matching industry (+1). Margins: every disclosed county aggregate (lines 2, 91, 92, 87, 12, 50, 59, 68, 75, 88, 89, 90, minus its disclosed leaves) and every state leaf total (state value minus disclosed counties). Disclosed county aggregates are reproduced to within BEA's own $1-4 thousand rounding except a handful of counties (all < 0.1 %) and state industry totals to within 0.02 % (exact figures in report.json); national sector totals equal the sum of BEA state rows. BEA combination areas (23 Virginia county + independent-city combinations, Maui + Kalawao) are split to Census 2023 counties pro rata to 2023 population (Census PEP vintage 2023). Totals are the sum of the 50 states + DC; BEA's US row also includes overseas federal government activity (the whole ~0.55 % gap is in line 83, government). Allocation to hexes: population-weighted within each county. gdp_usd = line 1 (all-industry total). Note: US county GDP is industry value added (taxes on production are inside industry value added), so both are GDP at market prices.

metrics.label: Median household income
metrics.description: Median annual household income, current US dollars of the survey year.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 2020-2024 5-year B19013_E001 (median household income in the past 12 months, 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars), county. Different survey years (2019 vs 2024 $) and income concepts: compare levels with care (no PPP adjustment applied).

metrics.label: Poverty rate
metrics.description: Share of people living below the national official poverty line.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 5-year B17001_E002 / B17001_E001 x 100 (people below the Census Bureau's income-based official poverty thresholds, by family size/composition; universe = people for whom poverty status is determined). The two national lines are very different absolute standards (the Sri Lankan line is far below the US thresholds), so rates are comparable only within each country.

metrics.label: People in poverty
metrics.description: Number of people below the national official poverty line.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 5-year B17001_E002.

metrics.label: Agriculture, forestry & fishing GVA (Food)
metrics.description: Gross value added of agriculture, forestry and fishing (ISIC A / NAICS 11), current US dollars.
metrics.method: USA 2025: BEA SAGDP2 state GDP of agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (line 3), current dollars, split to counties by each county's share of its state's NAICS 11 GDP in BEA CAGDP2 2024 (line 3; published county values, the latest county year). Counties sum exactly to the BEA state rows (50 states + DC). Proxy used only where BEA publishes no single-county value: SAGDP2 line 4 (farms) shared by the county's 2022 Census of Agriculture market value of products sold (Table 1; sales-share caveats as for ag_sales_usd) + line 5 (forestry, fishing, and related activities) shared by ACS 2020-2024 5-year employment in agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (C24030 lines 4 + 31, place of residence). (a) CAGDP2 cells suppressed '(D)': the state row minus the disclosed units is shared among the suppressed units in proportion to the proxy; (b) BEA combination areas (Virginia county + independent cities, Maui + Kalawao) are split to their member counties in proportion to the proxy. Hex allocation: cropland weight. Not the economy domain's gdp_agri_usd, which is the CAGDP2 2024 county release itself ($269.7 B; this SAGDP2 vintage gives $248.1 B for 2024 and $255.9 B for 2025).

metrics.label: Farm sales (market value of agricultural products sold)
metrics.description: Gross market value of crops, livestock and poultry sold by farms (gross output, not value added).
metrics.method: USDA NASS 2022 Census of Agriculture, county Table 1, 'Market value of agricultural products sold' ($1,000 x 1,000; gross sales of crops incl. nursery & greenhouse + livestock, poultry & their products, before expenses; county values sum to the published state totals). Withheld '(D)' county values: the state total minus the disclosed counties is shared among the withheld counties in proportion to their number of farms. Alaska is published only for 5 agricultural census districts whose borough composition is not given in the text files, so the Alaska state total is split to boroughs in proportion to BEA CAINC45 2022 farm cash receipts (non-zero for Aleutians West, Fairbanks North Star, Juneau, Kenai Peninsula, Matanuska-Susitna). Connecticut's 8 former counties are split to the 9 planning regions by the cropland inside each (former county x planning region) intersection (Census cb_2021 county polygons overlaid on cb_2023 planning regions). Units without a county column in the census tables get 0: Virginia independent cities other than Chesapeake, Suffolk and Virginia Beach (35), Baltimore city (MD), St. Louis city (MO) and Kalawao County (HI). District of Columbia: no value.

metrics.label: Tree & plantation crop share of agricultural land
metrics.description: Share of agricultural land under perennial tree / plantation crops (drives Plantation districts).
metrics.method: USA: 2022 Census of Agriculture land in orchards (Table 30: fruit and nut trees, citrus, vineyards, bearing + non-bearing acres) / total cropland (Table 1) x 100 - orchards are part of cropland, so the share is <= 100. Withheld '(D)' acres are filled per state from the state total minus disclosed counties: cropland shared by farms with cropland; orchards shared by the county's 2017 orchard acres (Table 30, else farms x the state median acres per orchard farm) and capped at the county's cropland. Alaska / Connecticut are split as for ag_sales_usd (both acreages with the same weights). Counties with less than 200 acres of cropland: no value. Definitional difference: the US denominator is cropland (excludes permanent pasture and woodland), the Sri Lankan one all agricultural land of holdings (incl. home gardens); the US numerator excludes berries, nurseries and Christmas trees.

metrics.label: Marine fish production / commercial landings
metrics.description: Commercial marine landings, metric tonnes (landed weight as reported by NOAA); comparable to Sri Lanka's marine fish production (district level).
metrics.method: NOAA FOSS commercial landings 2024: pounds summed over all species (incl. confidential aggregates) by state of landing x 0.45359237 / 1,000; Florida East + West coasts combined. Weights are used as published, without conversion to live weight: mollusc rows (clams, oysters, scallops, mussels; ~34 kt in 2024, about 1 % of the total) appear to be meat weight (e.g. sea scallops 21 M lb worth $332 M). 'Process at sea' landings (at-sea processors; 83 kt in 2024, almost all Pacific hake) are not attributed to any state and are excluded; Great Lakes commercial landings are not in FOSS after 2018 and are excluded (consistent with Sri Lanka's marine-only definition); states without marine landings = 0. Hex allocation: coast weight.

metrics.label: Commercial landings ex-vessel value
metrics.description: Ex-vessel value of commercial marine landings, current dollars.
metrics.method: NOAA FOSS commercial landings 2024: dollars summed by state (rows without a value contribute 0); same coverage rules as fish_catch_t.

metrics.label: Tropical cyclone passes (1980-2026)
metrics.description: Number of distinct tropical cyclones whose track passed within 100 km of the hex centre at tropical-storm strength or more, 1980 season to the latest (provisional) 2026 track.
metrics.method: IBTrACS since1980 list: main, PROVISIONAL and US-PROVISIONAL tracks (spurs dropped), points filtered to a box 5 deg around the country.  Wind = USA_WIND (1-min sustained, JTWC/NHC/CPHC) if reported, else WMO_WIND (agency-specific averaging, e.g. IMD 3-min, RSMC Tokyo 10-min).  A track point qualifies if NATURE is not ET (extratropical) or DS (disturbance) - TS (tropical), SS (subtropical), MX and NR are kept - and its wind is >= 34 kt.  Points with no reported wind never qualify (IBTrACS NATURE 'TS' means 'Tropical', any intensity, so it is not used as a strength proxy).  Consecutive points of a storm (<= 6 h apart) are densified to <= 10 km steps (great-circle interpolation of position; wind interpolated linearly when both fixes report one, otherwise the half-segment next to the fix with a wind takes that wind) so fast storms are not missed between 3-hourly fixes.  Count = distinct SIDs with any qualifying point within 100 km.  Exposure frequency at a point (not additive across hexes). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Strongest cyclone wind nearby (1980-2026)
metrics.description: Highest maximum sustained wind (knots) of any qualifying tropical cyclone while its track was within 100 km of the hex centre.
metrics.method: Max of the (interpolated) track-point wind over the qualifying points counted in cyclone_tracks.  USA_WIND (1-min) preferred, WMO_WIND fallback.  0 = no qualifying pass. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: M5+ earthquakes within 100 km (1976-2025)
metrics.description: Number of magnitude >= 5.0 earthquakes with epicentre within 100 km of the hex centre, 1 Jan 1976 - 31 Dec 2025 (any depth).
metrics.method: USGS ComCat FDSN CSV (preferred magnitude 'mag', any magType; eventtype=earthquake), deduplicated by event id across overlapping search boxes.  Exposure frequency at a point (not additive). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Largest earthquake within 100 km (1976-2025)
metrics.description: Largest magnitude among the M5+ earthquakes within 100 km of the hex centre.
metrics.method: Max of ComCat preferred magnitude over events counted in quakes_m5.  0 = no M5+ event. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Tsunami runup observations within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Number of NOAA NCEI tsunami runup / tide-gauge observations located within 25 km of the hex centre since 1900.
metrics.method: HazEL runups API, boxes around each country (no country filter, so cross-border runups count). Kept: year >= 1900 and source event validity >= 3 (probable or definite tsunami; seiches, doubtful and erroneous events dropped).  Each runup record counts once (one tsunami usually produces several records along a coast). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Tsunamis observed within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Number of distinct tsunamis (source events) with at least one NOAA NCEI runup / tide-gauge observation within 25 km of the hex centre since 1900.
metrics.method: Same runup records as tsunami_runups, counted by distinct tsunamiEventId instead of by record, so a heavily surveyed single event (e.g. the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami along Sri Lanka's coast) counts once.  A frequency measure, used in hazard_index. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Highest tsunami water height within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Maximum tsunami water height (runup or tide-gauge amplitude, metres) among the observations counted in tsunami_runups.
metrics.method: Max of runupHt over the kept runup records; records without a height are counted but do not set the maximum.  0 = no observation with a height. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Natural hazard index
metrics.description: Composite 0-100 exposure to tropical cyclones, strong earthquakes and tsunamis, on one scale for both countries (100 = most exposed).
metrics.method: Three event-frequency inputs: cyclone_tracks, quakes_m5 and tsunami_events (distinct tsunamis, not runup records).  For each input, a hex with 0 events scores 0; a hex with >= 1 event scores the mid-rank percentile of its value among all LAND hexes of BOTH countries (Sri Lanka res-6 + USA res-5 pooled) that have >= 1 event of that hazard: (n_below + 0.5 n_equal) / n_exposed.  Ranking among exposed hexes only keeps a single storm in 47 years from scoring like a hurricane coast just because most US hexes see none.  hazard_index = 100 x mean of the three scores, so a place exposed to only one hazard tops out near 33 and multi-hazard coasts (Hawaii, Alaska, California) score highest.  The reference distribution is pooled, so values are comparable between countries (inputs are radius counts, independent of hex size).  Each land hex counts once in the pool, so per km2 Sri Lanka's smaller res-6 tiles carry ~7x the weight of US res-5 tiles (Sri Lanka is ~5% of the pooled land hexes, but a larger share of the cyclone-exposed ones).  Floods, droughts, landslides, wildfire and tornadoes are not in this index (no consistent hex-level catalogue for both countries); see the admin tables for those.

metrics.label: FEMA National Risk Index score
metrics.description: FEMA National Risk Index composite risk score (0-100): a county's percentile-based score of NRI risk (expected annual loss from 18 natural hazards, scaled by social vulnerability and community resilience) relative to all counties in the NRI layer.
metrics.method: Field RISK_SCORE ('National Risk Index - Score - Composite') of the NRI Counties feature layer (NRI_VER 'December 2025'), joined on STCOFIPS = county GEOID (cb_2023 geography; no splitting needed).  The layer has 3,232 rows: the 3,144 counties of the 50 states + DC kept here plus 88 Puerto Rico / Island Area units (dropped), and FEMA's percentile ranks are over all 3,232.  US-only ranking, so it has no Sri Lankan counterpart.

metrics.label: Expected annual loss from natural hazards (FEMA NRI)
metrics.description: FEMA NRI expected annual loss, all 18 hazards: buildings + population (statistical value of life equivalence) + agriculture, in dollars per year.
metrics.method: Field EAL_VALT (Expected Annual Loss - Total - Composite; the 18 hazards are avalanche, coastal flooding, cold wave, drought, earthquake, hail, heat wave, hurricane, ice storm, landslide, lightning, inland flooding, strong wind, tornado, tsunami, volcanic activity, wildfire, winter weather), joined on STCOFIPS. metrics.label: Research works 2021-2025
metrics.description: Scholarly works (articles, reviews, books, conference papers, preprints, reports...) published 2021-2025 with an author affiliated to research institutions located in the hex.
metrics.method: OpenAlex institution points. research_works_5y = number of works published 2021-2025 of type article, review, book, book-chapter, conference-paper, preprint, report, dissertation, letter, data-paper, software-paper with an authorship affiliated to the institution (works?filter=authorships.institutions.id:<id>,publication_year:2021-2025,type:...; meta.count). Datasets, peer reviews, errata, editorials, conference abstracts, book reviews, paratext, software and 'other' are excluded (OpenAlex lists very large numbers of deposited datasets for a few US institutions; counts below). Column works_5y keeps the all-types counts_by_year total for reference. A co-authored work counts once for every participating institution, so sums over hexes or the nation exceed the number of distinct works; preprints and their published versions can both count. Parent organisations do not roll up their children in OpenAlex (works are counted on the institution id, not its lineage), so there is no hierarchy double counting. Points sit at the Wikidata campus coordinate (item with the institution's ROR ID, nearest P625 within 50 km of the OpenAlex point) or, failing that, at the OpenAlex/GeoNames city point of the institution's ROR record (column coord_source). Reconcile sums the points per hex. Sri Lanka: all OpenAlex institutions with country_code LK. United States: institutions with more than 200 lifetime works, which excludes only the long tail of small organisations. Build facts: 6,834 institution points (6,834 fetched; 4,148 at Wikidata campus coordinates, 2,686 at the OpenAlex city point); total 8,879,814 institution-works (all-types works_5y total 15,209,878). OpenAlex lists 35,768 institutions with country_code US (6,834 used) and 4,385,966 distinct research works 2021-2025 with a US affiliation, so the institution sum is x2.02 the distinct count; it also lists 1,826,941 US-affiliated datasets in the period (excluded); largest non-research totals per institution: Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory 1.20 M; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory 1.17 M.

metrics.label: University R&D expenditure (HERD FY2024)
metrics.description: Total R&D expenditures of the higher-education institution (all sources of funds).
metrics.method: NSF HERD FY2024 Table 5 'All R&D expenditures' (dollars in thousands x 1000), 50 states + DC. System subtotal rows are dropped (a row is a subtotal when it equals the sum of its indented children; superscript footnote markers removed). Institutions are matched to OpenAlex education/healthcare/nonprofit/facility/government institutions by normalised name within the same state (U./C./Inst./Sch./Med./St. expanded, SUNY/CUNY prefixes dropped): exact token match, then names that differ only by a place qualifier (after a comma, dash or 'at', or a state name), then fuzzy >= 0.86; one-to-one, greedy by score then R&D. Manual assignments (science.HERD_ASSIGN) cover renamed institutions, abbreviation clashes and system offices; where HERD reports campuses jointly (U. Maryland = College Park + Baltimore per Table 5 footnote b; U. Oklahoma = Norman + Health Sciences Center + Tulsa per footnote d; Texas A&M + Health Science Center; Penn State + Hershey; Vanderbilt + VUMC; Nebraska-Lincoln + UNMC; Dartmouth + Dartmouth-Hitchcock) the R&D is split in proportion to each campus's 2021-2025 research works (an estimate). Johns Hopkins U. includes the Applied Physics Laboratory (Laurel, MD); the APL amount published in footnote c goes to the APL point and the rest to the Homewood point. Matches are listed in herd_matches.csv. Build facts: 870 of 906 HERD institutions (50 states + DC) matched = 99.9% of $117.54 bn; top-100 matched 100/100; 63 manual assignments (71 OpenAlex pairs) and 1 footnote split(s) (2 pairs); 877 OpenAlex institutions carry R&D, total $117.41 bn.

metrics.label: Mean elevation
metrics.description: Mean height of the land (and inland-water) surface in the hex (DSM, metres above EGM2008 geoid).
metrics.method: Copernicus GLO-90 DSM pixels assigned to the H3 hex whose boundary contains the pixel centre (H3 polygons rasterised on each DEM tile grid). Both countries use the native 3 arc-sec tiles (~90 m N-S; E-W spacing widens north of 50N following the GLO tiling: 4.5 arc-sec at 50-60N, 6 at 60-70N, 9 at 70-80N), so values are comparable between Sri Lanka and the US. Statistics use pixels with DEM != 0 (land and inland-water surfaces, which the DEM flattens; ocean is 0 m and absent tiles are sea); hexes without such pixels get 0 m and 0 deg. Means are weighted by pixel area. DSM heights include canopy/buildings, relative to the EGM2008 geoid; 90 m pixels smooth sharp summits, so hex maxima sit somewhat below surveyed peak heights. Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land inside a US border hex is included).

metrics.label: Mean slope
metrics.description: Average terrain slope of land pixels in the hex (90 m DEM in both countries).
metrics.method: Copernicus GLO-90 DSM pixels assigned to the H3 hex whose boundary contains the pixel centre (H3 polygons rasterised on each DEM tile grid). Both countries use the native 3 arc-sec tiles (~90 m N-S; E-W spacing widens north of 50N following the GLO tiling: 4.5 arc-sec at 50-60N, 6 at 60-70N, 9 at 70-80N), so values are comparable between Sri Lanka and the US. Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land inside a US border hex is included). Slope = atan(|grad z|) from central differences (numpy.gradient) on the native 90 m DEM grid with metric pixel spacing (dx = deg x 111.32 km x cos(lat), dy = deg x 110.57 km), one-sided at tile edges, averaged (pixel-area weighted) over the hex's DEM != 0 pixels. The same grid is used in both countries because slope is strongly resolution dependent (on a 4x coarser, ~370 m grid the Sri Lankan hex slopes are ~0.57x the 90 m values); 30 m or lidar DEMs give steeper values still.

metrics.label: Land cover: Tree cover
metrics.description: Fraction (0-1) of the hex covered by ESA WorldCover class 10 'Tree cover'.
metrics.method: Share of the hex's pixels in WorldCover class 10 (Tree cover). WorldCover pixels (Sri Lanka: all native 10 m pixels; USA: the COG's 4x internal overview, 1/3000 deg ~ 40 m, which was built with mode resampling, so scattered minority classes are under-represented: against native 10 m pixels around 80 random US land hexes (mostly rural), built-up was -11% relative (max 0.5 percentage points per hex), shrub/wetland/moss -1 to -2%, other classes within +-0.5%; in dense urban hexes built-up is instead over-represented by ~2-3 points (Manhattan, Silicon Valley). Sri Lankan shares (10 m) have no such bias) are assigned to the hex containing their centre (rasterised H3 polygons); fractions are over the whole hex area, so the 11 classes sum to 1. Open ocean (no-data 0 inside tiles, or no tile at all) is counted as water (class 80). Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land included); the *_km2 weights are in-country only.

WorldCover pixels (Sri Lanka: all native 10 m pixels; USA: the COG's 4x internal overview, 1/3000 deg ~ 40 m, which was built with mode resampling, so scattered minority classes are under-represented: against native 10 m pixels around 80 random US land hexes (mostly rural), built-up was -11% relative (max 0.5 percentage points per hex), shrub/wetland/moss -1 to -2%, other classes within +-0.5%; in dense urban hexes built-up is instead over-represented by ~2-3 points (Manhattan, Silicon Valley). Sri Lankan shares (10 m) have no such bias) are assigned to the hex containing their centre (rasterised H3 polygons); fractions are over the whole hex area, so the 11 classes sum to 1. Open ocean (no-data 0 inside tiles, or no tile at all) is counted as water (class 80). Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land included); the *_km2 weights are in-country only.

metrics.label: Cropland area
metrics.description: Area of cropland (WorldCover class 40) inside the country part of the hex.
metrics.method: Cropland area (km2) = share of the hex's in-country WorldCover pixels (centre inside the COD-AB / Census cartographic boundary union) in class 40 x core land_km2 of the hex (WorldPop pixel-area crosswalk). Border hexes therefore exclude Canadian/Mexican land; water-ring hexes with land_km2 = 0 get 0. Hexes with land_km2 > 0 but no in-country WorldCover pixel at the processing resolution fall back to the whole-hex non-water shares. Intended as the 'cropland' allocation weight; note that civmap.reconcile currently derives its 'cropland' weight from the whole-hex lc_* fraction x piece land area instead, which under-weights part-sea coastal hexes (Sri Lanka national totals: built -13%, grass+shrub -5%, cropland -2% vs this column).

metrics.label: Mean annual temperature
metrics.description: Annual mean air temperature (WorldClim BIO1).
metrics.method: BIO1 (annual mean temperature, deg C) of the WorldClim 2.1 1970-2000 normals, nearest-pixel value at the centres of the hex's H3 children (res+2, 49 points/hex), averaged over points with data, on the 2.5 arc-min grid (~4.6 km) for both countries. Land hexes with no valid sample (coastal slivers) take the nearest valid pixel within 10 pixels (~46 km); open-water hexes and remote atolls (e.g. Northwestern Hawaiian Islands) with no valid sample are left empty.

metrics.label: Population density
metrics.description: People per km² of land (area inside the boundary, incl. inland water).
metrics.method: pop / land_km2

metrics.label: GDP per capita
metrics.description: GDP per resident at current prices.
metrics.method: Tiles: gdp_usd ÷ residents (tiles with ≥ 50 residents; equal to the population-weighted value of the units the tile overlaps). Admin units: unit GDP ÷ unit population. gdp_usd of the county/district divided by its 2023 population used by the core grid (US Census PEP vintage 2023; Sri Lanka DCS mid-2023 estimates via COD-PS). USA: BEA county GDP is workplace-based, so commuter and resource hubs (Manhattan, DC, oil counties such as Loving County TX with 43 residents) are strongly inflated. Sri Lanka: provincial GDP is workplace-based, but the district split uses LFS employment by place of residence, so commuting into Colombo district is NOT captured (Colombo likely understated, Gampaha/Kalutara overstated).
